question.text: 'Aranya Cat II AIF' has total commitments of INR 800 crore. Cumulative drawdowns to date are 40%. LP Mr. Rajesh Bansal has committed INR 20 crore. What is his remaining UNCALLED (uncommitted-yet-drawn) capital?

explanation.text: The Logic: Called so far = 40% x INR 20 cr = INR 8 crore. Remaining uncalled = INR 20 cr - INR 8 cr = INR 12 crore. This is Mr. Bansal's share of 'dry powder' at fund level. The Trap: Option A is called (not uncalled). Option C is the full commitment — ignores drawdown. Option D doubles commitment erroneously. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B test drawdown vs commitment; XIX-C often asks for uncalled/dry-powder which LPs track for liquidity planning. Manager's Pro-Tip: Uncalled capital is a real liability for LP treasury teams. Publish a rolling 90-day drawdown forecast in your quarterly letter — it reduces LP default risk and builds Manager credibility.
